websearch.worst: A: Jepsen's serializable G2-item finding is presented without noting it was a bug in 12.3 with a patch already committed for the next minor release
websearch.worst_summary_quote: PostgreSQL's "serializable" isolation level isn't serializable: it allows G2-item during normal operation.
websearch.worst_page_quote: A patch for the bug we found in serializability is scheduled for the next minor release, on August 13th
websearch.reader_gets_wrong: A reader would think current PostgreSQL Serializable still allows serialization anomalies (G2-item), when Jepsen reported a since-patched bug in 12.3.
websearch.notes: Official docs page was not among the Links (a PG10 mirror was); summary points to postgresql.org/docs/current. Summary also omits that Jepsen found G2-item under repeatable read. Fetched pages: jepsen, pgdash, crunchy mirror, hackorum, mkdev.

webfetch.fetch_prompt: From this PostgreSQL documentation page on transaction isolation, list the anomalies (e.g., dirty read, non-repeatable read, phantom read, serialization anomaly) that SERIALIZABLE prevents compared with REPEATABLE READ, and summarize how the docs describe each isolation level's guarantees.
webfetch.notes: Page 24383 chars, no truncation noted. Summary covers serialization anomaly, example, retry, unique-violation caveat, DEFERRABLE blocking. Omits only the read-only control-record example (minor).
